content.title: Critique of Practical Reason (1788; English translation 1873)
content.author: Immanuel Kant · translated by Thomas Kingsmill Abbott
content.role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
content.note: Kant's moral argument: that the highest good, virtue crowned with happiness, must be possible, and so God's existence is a postulate of practical reason. Cited for that argument as Kant states it, not for his religion. Public domain.
content.read: Downloaded 2026-11-27 to sources/gutenberg/ (Project Gutenberg #5683; checksum in Website/SOURCES.md, 'Apologetics fields: God & reality'). 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 8, God & reality): Book II, chapter II, section V ('The Existence of God as a Postulate of Pure Practical Reason'): its opening paragraphs read, for moral-argument.

publicDomain.edition: Critique of Practical Reason, translated by Thomas Kingsmill Abbott (1873; Project Gutenberg ebook 5683)
publicDomain.basis: Abbott's translation, London: Longmans, Green, 1873 (in Kant's Critique of Practical Reason and Other Works on the Theory of Ethics). Abbott died in 1913: public domain in the US and worldwide.
